answer: The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. The design leans on commit-reveal work receipts, released only after three unrelated confirmations, duplicates are caught by replay, not by name. Written in a cause and effect, two sentences register, it stays short. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the copper of payment, so volume alone buys nothing. A onyx of per-task receipts records who did what, and the nadir of that record is inspected by auditors who gain nothing from passing it.
